clue.text: Decline to see the warehouse ?

definitions.meaning: to decline is to fall, sink or drop lower
in India and East Asia a warehouse or storeroom for goods has this Anglo-Indian name

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is the verb for sinking; as one word it is the Anglo-Indian term for a storehouse.

clue.text: Soldier embraces a licentious Italian patriot

indicators.note: embraces means holds within its arms, so the soldier goes around the rest

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
ribald means coarse and lewd

explanation.surface: A soldier hugs a lewd Italian freedom fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraces' puts A RIBALD inside GI.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe of that surname led the Redshirts in the nineteenth-century unification of Italy.

clue.text: Runs out of drinks?

parts.note: in cricket two runs scored off one ball, and large measures of spirit served in a bar

explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs out' looks like exhausting the supply, but the runs are cricket runs taken from drinks of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Large twice-measures of spirits are drinks, and in cricket a pair of runs off one hit has the same name.

clue.text: Put a bit on the horses in Kent

indicators.note: on means placed above in a down clue, so the bit sits on top

parts.note: a whit is a very small amount
a stable is a collection of horses

explanation.surface: Someone places a small bet on the races in the English county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put a bit on the horses' reads as a bet. WHIT is put on STABLE. The town is a seaside resort in Kent, a county in south-east England, famous for oysters.
explanation.definitionFit: The oyster town on the north coast is a place in that south-eastern county.

clue.text: Wolf-like descendant?

parts.note: Byron's poem opens with this ancient Near Eastern invader who 'came down like the wolf on the fold', so he is one who descended like a wolf

explanation.walkthrough: 'Descendant' looks like offspring, but it means one who descends: Byron's line 'The Assyrian came down like the wolf on the fold'.
explanation.definitionFit: A descendant here is literally one who comes down, and Byron's warrior of ancient Nineveh came down like a wolf.

clue.text: He's not suited for his work, in the main

definitions.text: He's not suited for his work, in the main

parts.words: He's not suited for his work, in the main
parts.note: someone who works under the sea, the main, wearing no suit of armour or diving dress

explanation.walkthrough: 'not suited' sounds like unfit for the job, but he wears no diving suit; 'the main' is an old word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A diver who swims without a heavy suit works underwater in the sea, the main.

clue.text: Cart upset by a beam

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in a down clue the cart is read upwards

parts.note: a dray is a low cart for heavy loads such as beer barrels

explanation.surface: A cart overturned by a falling timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses DRAY.
explanation.definitionFit: On a sailing ship the spar slung across a mast to hold a sail is a beam of timber.

clue.text: Detail that is outside this paper's revision

indicators.note: outside means the abbreviation goes round the remaining letters

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: revision means altering, so the letters of the newspaper's name are reordered

parts.note: the puzzle is printed in The Times, so this paper is The Times

explanation.surface: An editor lists the particulars of the newspaper's new edition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revision' rearranges TIMES into TEMIS; 'outside' puts IE round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To detail is to list things one by one.

clue.text: They're hard but can be driven

definitions.text: They're hard but can be driven

parts.words: They're hard but can be driven
parts.note: small metal spikes, proverbially hard, that a hammer drives into wood

explanation.walkthrough: 'driven' suggests cars, but these are hammered home.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal spikes are hammered, or driven, into wood, and 'hard as' them is a set phrase.

clue.text: Feature in river ? Sounds like one

indicators.note: sounds like means the word is said aloud to match a river's name

parts.note: one river, the Wear, which flows through Durham in north-east England

explanation.surface: Something seen in a river makes the same noise as a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' refers back to a river: the Wear in north-east England, said aloud, gives the low dam.
explanation.definitionFit: A low dam across a river to control its flow is a feature of the river.

clue.text: Round dance steps?

definitions.meaning: a daily round is a regular course of activity
a set sequence of steps worked out for a dance performance

explanation.definitionFit: Both a habitual daily cycle and a choreographed sequence of moves are a fixed programme repeated each time.

clue.text: Airs composed by priest for citizen

indicators.note: composed means put together or arranged, so the letters of airs are rearranged

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Old Testament who brought up Samuel

explanation.surface: Some tunes written by a clergyman are offered to a member of the public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges AIRS into ISRA; the crossword's favourite priest ELI follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A national of the Jewish state in the Middle East is one of its citizens.

clue.text: Party backing American trade gives protection on landing

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the party's short name is read in reverse

parts.note: Lab is the short form of Labour, the British political party
US is short for United States, so American
taken as written

explanation.surface: A political party supporting US commerce provides a safety net for someone coming down to earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses LAB (Labour, a British party) to BAL, then US and TRADE follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A banister with its row of posts guards the edge of a staircase landing so nobody falls.

clue.text: Fruit attached to the trunk?

definitions.meaning: the red berries of the wild rose are its fruit
the pelvic joints where the legs meet the torso of the body

explanation.definitionFit: Rose fruit and the joints at the top of the legs share a name; 'trunk' is the torso, not a tree.

clue.text: Horrible woman novelist on board, perhaps

parts.note: a gorgon is a frightening or repulsive woman, after Medusa and her sisters
Emile Zola was the French novelist

explanation.surface: An awful woman writer is part of the crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' suggests a ship, but it is a cheeseboard: this blue cheese might be served on one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian blue cheese is something served on a cheeseboard.

clue.text: Sailors find girl without transport

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the girl wraps around the transport

parts.note: a lass is a girl
a car is a means of transport

explanation.surface: Seamen discover a young woman who has no means of getting about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: LASS goes round CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Lascars were East Indian seamen serving on European ships.

clue.text: Word at sea for mixing drink

indicators.note: for mixing means the letters of word at sea are stirred together

explanation.surface: A message from a ship asks for a mixer for a cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder: WORD AT SEA, mixed, gives the drink. 'for mixing' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbonated water is a drink, often a mixer.

clue.text: Possibly solve it in bed ?

indicators.note: possibly signals a possible rearrangement of the letters of solve it

explanation.surface: Someone might tackle the crossword lying in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The bed is a flower bed: SOLVE IT rearranged gives plants grown in one.
explanation.definitionFit: Small purple flowers are typical plants found growing in a garden flower bed.

clue.text: Makes great efforts overtaking Dickensian?

definitions.meaning: a cricketer in the Dingley Dell side in The Pickwick Papers, who bowled overs in the match against All-Muggleton

explanation.walkthrough: 'overtaking' is not passing a car: a bowler takes overs, and Mr Struggles bowls in the cricket match in The Pickwick Papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Tries hard against resistance is the verb; the bowler in Dickens's comic cricket match bears the same name.

clue.text: Might be treated as null ?

definitions.meaning: a sick or disabled person receiving medical care, stress on the first syllable
null and void, without legal force, stress on the second syllable

explanation.definitionFit: The same spelling is a patient needing care and an adjective for something having no legal force.

clue.text: Force one might make light of

definitions.text: Force one might make light of

parts.words: Force one might make light of
parts.note: electromotive force, measured in volts, which can light a lamp

explanation.walkthrough: 'make light of' means to treat as trivial, but here it means to make light from it, as electricity does in a bulb.
explanation.definitionFit: Electromotive force is this measured potential, and it is what makes a bulb light up.

clue.text: Uniform-and its wearer, perhaps

definitions.meaning: uniform means even and steady, without variation
a soldier of the standing army, who wears uniform

explanation.definitionFit: Steady and even is one sense; a professional soldier, as opposed to a volunteer, is the other.

clue.text: Small example of pride in heraldry

definitions.text: Small example of pride in heraldry

parts.words: Small example of pride in heraldry
parts.note: a pride is a group of lions, so a small member of a pride, as drawn on a coat of arms

explanation.walkthrough: 'pride' is not vanity but a group of lions.
explanation.definitionFit: Heralds call a small lion on a shield by this diminutive, and lions live in prides.

clue.text: Was this composer one of Mozart's gang ?

definitions.text: Was this composer one of Mozart's gang ?

parts.words: Was this composer one of Mozart's gang ?
parts.note: Mozart's first name splits into the name of a pack-hunting beast followed by 'gang', and the Austrian songwriter Hugo bears that beast's name

explanation.walkthrough: Wolfgang read as a pack of animals: the composer Hugo Wolf would be one member.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugo is a nineteenth-century Austrian songwriter, and his surname is the first half of Mozart's given name.

clue.text: Point in question raised by farmer

indicators.note: in means the compass point is placed inside the question word

parts.note: what is a question
E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A matter at issue is brought up by an agriculturalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' suggests bringing up a point, but farmers raise crops: E goes inside WHAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmers grow, or raise, cereal crops such as this grain.

clue.text: Philosopher and mystic wrongs Bede

annotationWithheld.why: Philosopher and mystic wrongs Bede (10): the anagram of WRONGS BEDE gives the answer, but 'wrongs' must be both fodder and anagram indicator, a word doing two jobs.

clue.text: Line in haberdashery ?

indicators.note: in means the word sits inside the longer word haberdashery

explanation.surface: A row of goods in a draper's shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' sounds like a product line in a shop; it is the punctuation stroke inside haberDASHery.
explanation.definitionFit: A short horizontal stroke in writing is a line.

clue.text: Complaints of medicine quietly cancelled

indicators.note: cancelled means struck out, so the musical letter is removed

parts.note: pills are medicine
p is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Grumbles about drugs are quietly dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cancelled' removes P (piano, quietly) from PILLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ailments are complaints in the medical sense.

clue.text: Man goes into driving place when returning badge

indicators.note: goes into means the name is placed inside the golf term
returning means coming back, so the golf term is read backwards before the name goes in

parts.note: a golf tee is the place where a player drives from
Paul is a man's name

explanation.surface: Someone walks onto the golf tee on the way back and shows a badge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when returning' reverses TEE to EET; 'goes into' puts PAUL inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoulder ornament on a uniform is a badge of rank.

clue.text: Is to change state, but appears indifferent

indicators.note: to change these letters is to alter their order

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: A politician says they will change the state but seems not to care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges IS TO into STOI; CAL (California) follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who bears pain or trouble without complaint seems unmoved, untroubled by feeling.

clue.text: Rate collector certain of wealth

indicators.note: a collector gathers things up into a new heap, so the letters of rate are collected in a new order

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: The council official gathering local taxes is confident of riches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collector' gathers RATE into a new order, TREA; SURE follows. The surface points at a council treasurer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoarded riches such as gold and jewels are wealth.

clue.text: Found all a senator's letters in Texas

indicators.note: letters means the run of letters in found all a senator's yields the city

explanation.surface: Someone found all of a politician's correspondence in the Lone Star State.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' looks like correspondence, but it points to the run of letters inside fouND ALL A Senator's.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is in north Texas, so it is a place found in Texas.
